newsitem.title: USA: Nike stock plunges after warning on earnings.
newsitem.headline: Nike stock plunges after warning on earnings.

text.p: Nike Inc. stock fell more than 13 percent Thursday after the company said profits for the current quarter would be far less than Wall Street had expected.
Nike tumbled $8.625 to $55.375 and was the most active issue with more than 19 million shares changing hands in consolidated trading on the New York Stock Exchange.

The collapse came after the athletic footwear and apparel company said it expected net income equal to 51 cents to 56 cents a share for its fourth quarter, which ends on May 31, about 20 percent below the Wall Street consensus of 69 cents.
"It's a pretty significant miss," said analyst Shawn Narancich of brokerage D.A. Davidson & Co. in Great Falls, Mont.
Nike blamed the shortfall on several factors, including a shift in Europe to more advance ordering, a shortage of apparel inventories and some cancellations in the United States.

"If you look at these items individually none of these really are that significant to the quarter," Nike Chief Financial Officer Bob Falcone told analysts in a conference call. "But collectively, when you add them all up, it becomes a significant issue at the top line."
The Beaverton, Ore.-based company also said earnings will be affected by a charge of $18 million, or 4 cents a share, to shut down a Canadian skate manufacturing facility.

Falcone said despite the shortfall, Nike is ending an "outstanding" year with revenues and earnings up at least 40 percent. Last year the company saw growth of about 36 percent with earnings of $545 million on revenues of $6.5 billion.
But company executives and analysts said Nike's growth inevitably will slow in the year ahead, particularly in the mature U.S. footwear market.

"I think we have a very difficult next six months, primarily because of the extraordinary growth the company experienced last year in its domestic footwear business," said Shelly Hale Young of Hambrecht & Quist, who was among several analysts who downgraded the stock earlier this year.

Nike stock has dropped more than 35 percent from its all-time high of $76.375 in February, mainly because of concerns about the slowing U.S. footwear market. Thursday's drop more than gave up gains of the previous two sessions, when Nike had risen sharply on speculation billionaire Warren Buffett was building a stake.

Nike's U.S. footwear sales grew 24 percent last year and have grown another 38 percent this year despite the relatively mature market. The sports marketing giant has taken share from its biggest rivals, Reebok International Ltd., Converse Inc. and L.A. Gear Inc., acording to Sporting Goods Intelligence, an industry newsletter.
Analysts expect Nike's U.S. footwear sales to grow only about 5 percent in the coming year.
"It's just logical they're not going to be able to continue growing that market share by 20 to 40 percent a year," said Narancich.
Nike executives reiterated that they expect annual sales growth of 15 percent to 18 percent, as rapidly increasing international sales help offset slowing domestic growth.

But analyst Mike Conn of Grutal & Co. said he was concerned by Falcone's comment that European sales for the current quarter will be about $100 million short of expectations because of shipment timing and a shift in ordering patterns.
"I will be watching closely to see if it really is a one-time aberration," he said.
Nike and Buffett's Berkshire Hathaway Inc. have declined to comment on the rumours of the investor's interest in the footwear maker.
